title: Conservative points detect flatness over an arbitrary ring sheaf
statement: Work in the universe convention [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $(\mathcal C,J)$ be a small site, let $R$ be a sheaf of commutative rings on it, and let $M$ be a sheaf of $R$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Let $\{p_i\}_{i\in I}$ be a set-indexed family of points of $\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C,J)$: each $p_i$ is a geometric morphism $\mathbf{Set}\to\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C,J)$ [def-trf-geometric-morphism]. Assume that the inverse-image functors $p_i^{-1}$ jointly reflect isomorphisms of sheaves of sets. Give $R_i=p_i^{-1}R$ its induced commutative ring structure and $M_i=p_i^{-1}M$ its induced $R_i$-module structure, by applying $p_i^{-1}$ to the ring and module operations using its finite-product comparisons. Then $M$ is flat as a sheaf of $R$-modules [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules] if and only if $M_i$ is a flat $R_i$-module [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map] for every $i\in I$. The ring sheaf $R$ need not be constant, and no quasi-coherence or finiteness assumption on $M$ is imposed.

proof.text: For each $i$, choose the normalized presentation $s_i$ supplied by [def-sfb-ringed-site-point], with ring $R_i$ and module functor $S_i$. Its prescribed transport of operations is exactly the finite-product transport in the statement, so $S_i(M)=M_i$ up to the specified module identification. If $M$ is flat, [lem-sfb-ringed-site-point-flat] gives flatness of $S_i(M)$ over $R_i$, for every $i$.

Assume every $M_i$ is flat. Let $K=(A\xrightarrow{f}B\xrightarrow{g}C)$ be any complex of $R$-module sheaves exact at $B$. Regard it as a cochain complex in degrees $0,1,2$, zero elsewhere [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules], and write $M[0]$ for $M$ in degree zero. Exactness of $S_i$ [lem-sfb-ringed-site-point-exact] makes $S_i(A)\to S_i(B)\to S_i(C)$ exact. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-flat-tensor-exact] over the commutative ring $R_i$ with flat module $S_i(M)=M_i$. Thus $S_i(A)\otimes_{R_i}M_i\to S_i(B)\otimes_{R_i}M_i\to S_i(C)\otimes_{R_i}M_i$ is exact at its middle term. By the signed-total formula [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves], this is degree-one exactness of $\operatorname{Tot}(S_i(K)\otimes_{R_i}S_i(M[0]))$. The isomorphism of complexes in [lem-sfb-ringed-site-point-tensor], applied to $K,M[0]$, proves degree-one exactness of $S_i(\operatorname{Tot}(K\otimes_R M[0]))$. No naturality assertion beyond that complex isomorphism is needed.

Exactness is reflected by these $S_i$: for any three-term module complex $L=(L^0\xrightarrow{a}L^1\xrightarrow{b}L^2)$ put $H=\ker(b)/\operatorname{im}(a)$ in the abelian module-sheaf category [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. An exact functor preserves kernels, cokernels and hence images, so [lem-sfb-ringed-site-point-exact] identifies $S_i(H)$ with $\ker S_i(b)/\operatorname{im}S_i(a)$. If every $S_i(L)$ is exact at its middle, then $S_i(H)=0$. By the underlying-set identification in [def-sfb-ringed-site-point], every $p_i^{-1}$ sends the map $|H|\to|0|$ to a bijection. Joint reflection of isomorphisms makes this map an isomorphism of set sheaves; its inverse preserves the unique zero module structure, so $H=0$. Thus $L$ is exact at $L^1$. This is the kernel-quotient argument behind Tag 05V3.

Apply step 3 to $L=\operatorname{Tot}(K\otimes_R M[0])$, using step 2. The total formula [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves] gives $L=(A\otimes_R M\to B\otimes_R M\to C\otimes_R M)$: only the summands with second degree zero survive and their differential is $d_K\otimes1$. Hence tensoring with $M$ preserves exactness of every three-term complex, including those with an endpoint zero. It is additive: on local pure tensors $(f+f')\otimes1$ sends $a\otimes m$ to $f(a)\otimes m+f'(a)\otimes m$; the equality extends by bilinearity and sheafification [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. It therefore preserves short exact sequences, which is exactness of this additive functor. By [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules], $M$ is flat.

proof_origin.place: Tag 05VC (lemma-check-flat-stalks): forward direction by stalk flatness; converse by tensor-stalk comparison and conservative exactness. The kernel-quotient argument spells out the latter, and complexes concentrated in three degrees use the existing total-tensor interface.

Step 1: def-sfb-ringed-site-point gives existence of normalized presentations and the identification S_i(M)=M_i, then lem-sfb-ringed-site-point-flat gives the forward direction. Step 2: point exactness plus the Mathlib leaf lem-weil-pbc-flat-tensor-exact over R_i; the Tot formula collapses to (-)⊗M_i because S(0)=0; the point-tensor complex isomorphism carries degree-1 exactness across. Step 3 is correctly elementary: S_i(H)=0, so p_i^{-1}|H| is a singleton, and joint reflection gives H=0; the empty family also works. Advisory: the existing lem-sfb-ringed-site-point-acyclic could be cited here instead. Step 4: the triples (0,A,B),(A,B,C),(B,C,0) give preservation of short exact sequences, which is def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules. Duplicate search: the kflat-stalk-criterion is the K-flat analogue and not a duplicate; etale-flat-geometric-fibers is the constant-coefficient case. No cycle in the 152-node closure.
